1	# Rules: Architecture
2	
3	- **R-p0j.** A project has one architecture at most, as it has one design system and one app shell.
4	- **R-c2m.** Every design, build and fix agent reads the architecture's principles, and the parts its change reaches, before it changes anything.
5	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/architecture*
6	- **R-h9w.** An agent whose change would go against the architecture proposes a decision on its branch, rather than making the change without saying so.
7	- **R-7tq.** A proposed decision is accepted when the branch that proposed it is merged into main, and agents on other branches don't see it before then.
8	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/architecture/decisions/:decision*
9	  *proposed*
10	- **R-4vx.** After every turn that changes code, the changed files are checked against the architecture, and a build or fix agent is told what doesn't match with its next message.
11	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/architecture @ drifted*
12	- **R-k5e.** A part may use the parts its file says it may, in its own layer or below it; any other use is reported, and so is a file no part names or a named file that isn't there.
13	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/architecture/parts/:part @ drifted*
14	  *proposed*
15	- **R-w8d.** Decisions are listed newest first.
16	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/architecture/decisions*
17	  *proposed*

text:
1	# Architecture - notes
2	
3	A fourth kind of design, besides features, the design system and the shell:
4	**the project's architecture**, kept as markdown files that agents read and
5	shown to the team on the project's Architecture pages, the way the design
6	system's gallery shows the system. Prelude's own architecture (from
7	`CLAUDE.md` and `docs/plan.md`) is the sample data.
8	
9	This design is those pages: views at Prelude's own URLs
10	(`/f/:folder/architecture/…`), with states shaped as Prelude's model of the
11	files would be.
12	
13	## Decided (2026-10-22, with the person)
14	
15	- **A design of `"kind": "architecture"`, one per project** (R-p0j), like the
16	  system and the shell. Its sessions shape it ("draft it from the code").
17	- **Prelude reads the files itself**, as it reads RULES.md, so nothing is
18	  written twice (D-e8y in the sample). The real architecture design will
19	  have no states; this design's states stand in for what Prelude reads.
20	- **Markdown, a file per thing**, in the design's `architecture/` folder (as
21	  the system's is `system/`):
22	  - `overview.md`: a summary, the layers in order, the principles (title, why);
23	  - `parts/<id>.md`: a header (title, layer, kind: module / process / outside,
24	    `files` globs, `uses` part ids), then sections: Responsible for, Not its
25	    job, Owns;
26	  - `decisions/<id>.md`: a header (title, status, date, parts, supersedes),
27	    then Context, Decision, Consequences. Ids are `D-` + three random
28	    characters, so branches never clash;
29	  - `flows/<id>.md`: a title, a summary, numbered steps each starting with
30	    the part's id.
31	  Prelude prepares what's derived: each part's "used by", decisions and
32	  findings, and the map's layers.
33	- **Proposed decisions are accepted by merging** (R-7tq): an agent's
34	  proposal is reviewed with its branch, and Prelude marks it accepted at
35	  merge (as it clears a route's `from`).
36	- **Agents use it** (R-c2m, R-h9w): ever

1	// A project's architecture (prelude/architecture): a design of "kind":
2	// "architecture", one per project (R-p0j), kept as markdown files that agents
3	// read before they change anything (R-c2m) and that Prelude reads to show
4	// them on the project's Architecture pages (D-e8y). Nothing is written twice:
5	// the files are the one source, and what's derived (each part's "used by",
6	// decisions and findings, the map's layers) is prepared here.
7	//
8	// The files, in the design's architecture/ folder (the format the drafting
9	// agent is told: architecturePrompt in agent.js):
10	//
11	//   overview.md          # title, a summary, "## Layers" (a numbered list, top
12	//                        to bottom) and "## Principles" ("- **Title.** Why.")
13	//   parts/<id>.md        # title, then a header of "key: value" lines (layer,
14	//                        kind: module | process | outside, short, files: globs,
15	//                        uses: part ids), a summary, and "## Responsible for",
16	//                        "## Not its job", "## Owns" lists
17	//   decisions/<id>.md    # title, a header (status, date, parts, supersedes),
18	//                        then "## Context", "## Decision", "## Consequences"
19	//   flows/<id>.md        # title, a summary, numbered steps "part-id: text",
20	//                        and an optional "decisions:" header
21	//
22	// The check (R-4vx, R-k5e; D-r0k): after every turn that changes code, the
23	// code is read again - each file's imports (JavaScript and TypeScript, so
24	// far), each file mapped to its part by `files` - and these are reported: a
25	// use a part doesn't say it may make, a use of a part in a layer above, a
26	// code file no part names, and a named file that isn't there. A file is
27	// expected to belong to a part when it's under a folder a part's glob names
28	// (server/views/** covers server/views/, recursively), or beside a file a
29	// part names (server/main.js covers server/'s own files).

I've built the part page. I haven't seen it render yet; Prelude's next check will show whether it does.

**What changed**
- **The view:** `server/views/architecture/part.eta` is the design's markup, element for element. It needed one partial the app didn't have yet, `_part-links.eta`, so I moved that over too. The design system already has every class the page uses, so no styles were added.
- **The route:** `/f/:folder/architecture/parts/:part` is now answered in `server/main.js`, next to the overview. Its model is the matching part from the overview's existing model. That model already had the shape the states use, including used by, decisions and findings, so I didn't add any new model code. A fragment request gets the page alone; otherwise it renders in the app layout. A part id that doesn't exist gets the app's usual "Not found" page.
- **routes.json:** the route now points at `@app/server/views/architecture/part`.
- **R-k5e:** the check in `server/architecture.js` already reports each use the rule covers:
  - a use the part's file doesn't allow
  - a use of a part in a higher layer
  - a code file that no part names
  - a named file that isn't there

  So I only removed the rule's *proposed* line.
- **`architecture-checked`:** this was already sent after a turn's check, down the app's live channel. The design's part page doesn't listen for it, so the event needed nothing new.
- **NOTES.md:** updated to say the part page is built and the decision, flow and Decisions pages still aren't.

**Before you approve, look at:**
- The **drifted** state of the part page (the Design host part): the warning box listing what doesn't match.
- An outside part, such as Claude CLI: it should show the "What it does is its own…" line instead of the job card.
- A gap in the check: it only reports a missing file when the part names an exact path. A pattern like `server/foo/**` that matches no files at all isn't reported. If R-k5e should catch that too, I'll add it.
